title: How To Transform A Difficult Class
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin challenges the common instinct to lower expectations for a difficult class, arguing the opposite approach actually works. He explains that easing standards backfires because it's human nature to settle for the lower bar a teacher sets, sends students the demoralizing message that they're not capable of more, and causes them to lose respect for a teacher unwilling to hold them accountable. Rather than appeasing, he recommends raising expectations higher than students have ever experienced, becoming a stickler for small details as proof they matter, and pairing that rigor with genuine care, strong instruction, and consistent praise. The core claim is that students will rise — or fall — to whatever expectation is set for them, so teachers who believe in their students' capacity and act on that belief get it back in the form of real transformation.
points: Lowering standards for a difficult class is a virtual guarantee that behavior worsens rather than improves.
Students naturally settle for whatever bar a teacher sets, rarely raising it above what's expected of them.
Accepting less sends students the message they're not good enough, and they come to believe and fulfill that lowered expectation.
Failing to hold a difficult class accountable at the same level as any other class causes students to lose respect for the teacher.
The recommended response is to raise the bar higher than ever, sweat small details, and combine that rigor with genuine care and instruction.
quotes: The most common approach to an especially difficult class is to lower the bar.
It’s natural human tendency to choose the easier road when given the chance. Unless challenged, few students in a difficult class (or school) will hold themself to a higher standard.

When your actions prove that you don’t believe they’re capable of more or better, both academically and behaviorally, they accept it as truth. They predictably fulfill the prophecy you set for them , thus giving you exactly what you expect.
And far from meeting you halfway, your students will push and push until there are no more consequences for any misbehavior. Invertebrate teachers get crushed in challenging environments.

So what should you do? The opposite. You raise the bar, higher than they’ve ever experienced. You become a stickler for the little things to show your students that they do matter and that they are worth it.
Challenge your students every minute of the day. Be worthy of their respect. Love them, provide great instruction, and offer them a new and hopeful prophecy to fulfill.
